summary: A Yes vote establishes a 7% utility users' tax to fund city services, with an exemption for low-income residents.

tax.text: A Yes vote on Measure Q would establish a 7% utility users tax to fund public safety, infrastructure repairs, and other city services.
tax.quote: shall the City of Marina’s measure establishing a 7% utility users’ tax with low-income rates, generating approximately $3,830,000 annually until ended by voters, requiring spending disclosures, audits, all funds spent locally, be adopted?

tax.text: The No on Measure Q campaign urges voters to reject Marina's proposed 7% utility users' tax, arguing it would be the highest rate on the Monterey Peninsula and would weigh most on working families.
tax.quote: You'll be paying the highest utility tax rate on the Peninsula
